title: 12-hour and 24-hour time
keyIdea: A clock face shows only 12 hours, so each time happens twice a day: once in the morning (am) and once after midday (pm). The 24-hour clock gives every hour its own number from 00 to 23 and always uses four digits. To change a pm time to 24-hour time, add 12 to the hour: 3:45 pm is 15:45. Morning hours keep their number with a zero in front: 9:10 am is 09:10. To go back, take 12 away from hours 13 to 23: 19:30 is 7:30 pm. Midnight is 00:00 and midday is 12:00.
familyTip: Look at a train or bus timetable, a TV guide or the clock on a cooker or phone set to 24-hour time. Take turns saying each time in 12-hour time with am or pm, and check by asking: is that before or after lunch?

visual.caption: Is each time am (before midday) or pm (after midday)? Drag each card, or tap it and then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag a marker through one day, write pm times in 24-hour form, match cards, sort midnight and midday, and read a train timetable.

kid: A clock face has the numbers 1 to 12. The short hand goes round twice every day. So 3 o’clock comes once in the night and once in the afternoon. We write am for times from midnight to midday, and pm for times from midday to midnight.

The 24-hour clock does not start again after midday. It keeps counting: 13, 14, 15, all the way to 23. Then midnight is 00:00 and a new day starts. A 24-hour time always has four digits, like 07:30 or 18:05.

To change a pm time into 24-hour time, add 12 to the hour. 4:20 pm is 4 + 12 = 16, so it is 16:20. Morning times keep the same hour, with a zero in front if needed: 9:05 am is 09:05. The minutes never change.

To go back, take 12 away from any hour from 13 to 23 and write pm. 19:30 is 19 − 12 = 7, so 7:30 pm. Be careful with 12 and 00: 12:15 is just after midday (12:15 pm), but 00:15 is just after midnight (12:15 am).
adult: Ages 8 to 9. The National Curriculum in England asks Year 4 pupils to read, write and convert time between analogue and digital 12- and 24-hour clocks. Year 5 and 6 pupils use the skill to read timetables and work out durations. Conventions follow the NCETM Year 4 guidance and the UK government style guide: 24-hour times use four digits with a colon (09:10, 15:45), midnight is 00:00 at the start of a day and midday is 12:00.

The lab has five tasks. Learners drag a marker along a day strip while an analogue clock, a 12-hour time and a 24-hour time all follow it. They write three 12-hour times in 24-hour form, using +12 only for pm. They match 24-hour cards to 12-hour cards, avoiding two decoys. They sort the 00 and 12 hours, then answer two train timetable questions.

Common mistakes. Many children drop the first digit instead of taking away 12, so 19:30 becomes 9:30 pm. Others add 10 instead of 12, add 12 to morning times, or forget the leading zero (writing 9:10 for 09:10). The 00 and 12 hours are the hardest: 12:20 is after midday but 00:20 is after midnight. In timetables, a 17 can be misread as 7 pm.

practice.prompt: Write {h}:30 pm in 24-hour time. What number is the hour?
practice.hint: It is after midday, so add 12 to the hour. The minutes stay the same.

practice.prompt: A 24-hour clock shows {h}:00. What is the hour on a 12-hour clock?
practice.hint: Hours from 13 to 23 are pm. Take away 12.
Morning hours keep their number. Use four digits.
practice.explain: 8:15 am is in the morning, so the hour stays 8, written 08:15. 20:15 would be 8:15 pm.

practice.hint: The 00 hour is the first hour after midnight.
practice.explain: 00:40 is 40 minutes after midnight, which is 12:40 am. 12:40 pm is 40 minutes after midday.

practice.prompt: Leo says 18:00 is 8 pm. What is right?
practice.hint: Do not just drop the 1. Take away 12.
practice.explain: 18 − 12 = 6, so 18:00 is 6 pm. Dropping the first digit gives the wrong hour.

pool.hint: pm means add 12 to the hour.
pool.explain: 3 + 12 = 15, so 3:45 pm is 15:45. 03:45 is in the night and 13:45 is 1:45 pm.
19 − 12 = 7, and hours after 12 are pm, so 19:30 is 7:30 pm.

pool.prompt: A film starts at {h}:00 pm and lasts 2 hours. What hour does it end, in 24-hour time?
pool.hint: Change the start to 24-hour time by adding 12, then add the 2 hours.

pool.prompt: How many hours is it from 09:00 to {h}:00?
pool.hint: Both times are in 24-hour time, so you can take away the hours.
pool.explain: Both are 24-hour times, so {h} − 9 = {=h-9} hours have passed.
Midday is 12:00. Midnight is 00:00 at the start of a day.

pool.prompt: A train leaves at 17:15. Is that before or after 6 pm?
pool.hint: Take 12 away from 17, then compare with 6 pm.
pool.explain: 17 − 12 = 5, so 17:15 is 5:15 pm, which is before 6 pm (18:00).

pool.hint: Is the 12 hour just after midnight or just after midday?
pool.explain: 12:20 is 20 minutes after midday, so it is 12:20 pm. 00:20 would be 12:20 am.

pool.prompt: Which time is written correctly in 24-hour time?
pool.hint: 24-hour times use four digits and no am or pm.
pool.explain: 06:05 has four digits and no am or pm. 6:5 is missing digits and 6:05 am is 12-hour time.

pool.hint: It is still the morning, so the hour does not change.
pool.explain: 11:10 am is before midday, so the hour stays 11: 11:10. 23:10 is 11:10 pm.
